frequency_question: What proportion of heavily contested executive nominations are successfully confirmed by the U.S. Senate?
membership_rule: Nominees to cabinet or high-profile sub-cabinet/agency head positions (FDA, CDC, HHS, Surgeon General) who faced organized opposition from at least one major political party in the Senate, examined between 2000 and 2024.

cases.name: John Tower Secretary of Defense Nomination
Tom Daschle HHS Nomination (Withdrawn before vote)
Robert Califf FDA Commissioner Nomination (2nd time)

coverage_note: 7 named; believed roughly 12 in total matching high-friction criteria over the period.
known_gaps: Excludes lower-tier subagency posts that rarely attract Senate floor fights.
skeleton: Contested major health and executive nominations categorized by Senate margin closeness and executive political capital.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 7 named high-friction historical cases
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as Senate confirmation norms and filibuster/cloture rules remain consistent.
